title: Localization compliance checklist and contract scoping (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working checklist and scoping note to align legal, sales, and ops on what we can promise in contract language for customers who require local-data residency (aka region-bound data handling). Focus is on practical enforcement, minimal operational burden, and clear fallback behavior to reduce SLA risk.

Scope & audience:
- Audience: Solutions, Legal, SRE, Private Deployment PMs, Account teams.
- Applies to: Private deployments (VPC / on-prem) and Dedicated tenants where customer requires region-restricted processing and storage.
- Not in scope: Hosted free-tier customers and ephemeral dev sandboxes (unless explicitly requested).

High-level approach summary (one-liner):
Offer a graded set of contract commitments that map to enforceable operator controls: (1) Storage residency only; (2) Compute + storage residence; (3) Auditable region pins with telemetry and per-request locality evidence. Each step increases operational cost and test burden.

Quick operational checklist (initial items):
- Identify dataset boundaries: which artifacts must stay in-region? (model weights, KV-cache dumps, logs, user payloads)
- Deployment topology: single-region private or multi-region with strict routing?
- Network boundaries and egress controls: ensure VPC routes, NAT rules, and firewall policies prevent cross-region egress from pinned services.
- Key management: ensure KMS/HSM is region-scoped; verify no cross-region key replication.
- Audit trail: enable request-level routing logs, node metadata, and storage location metadata for >= 90 days (customer-configurable).
- Evidence export: define format for "residency proof" (timestamped bucket+object list + node id + signed statement).
- Fallback policy: define acceptable fallback regions and auto-notify thresholds when local capacity exhausted.

Suggested contract language snippets (editable):
- Storage-only: "Customer Data at Rest will be stored in the region(s) specified in Schedule A. Redwood will not intentionally transfer Customer Data outside the specified region(s) except for transient caching necessary for performance or availability; such transfers will be logged and disclosed monthly."
- Compute+Storage: "Processing of Customer Data will occur within the specified region(s) unless Customer expressly permits fallback to alternative region(s) listed in Schedule B. Fallback will only be used under capacity or outage conditions and will be subject to the notification and mitigation procedures in Section X."
- Auditable Pin: "Redwood will provide an immutable, signed residency report for each calendar month, including per-request routing evidence for a representative sample (up to N requests per day) and storage object location indexes."

Operational constraints & cost signals:
- Single-region hard pinning requires overprovisioning for high-availability; recommend minimum 99% capacity commitment or explicit burst allowances.
- KV cache reuse across regions conflicts with strict per-region compute unless cache is region-sharded; quantify extra memory footprint per shard.
- Quantization/optimizations: some kernels are only available on specific GPU types and may force placement outside requested region; surface these limitations in SOW.

Telemetry and verification plan:
- Minimal telemetry required to evidence compliance: request_id, ingress node id, routed-region tag, timestamp, storage_destination (bucket+path), signing key id.
- Implement a nightly job that compiles the residency index and signs it with our platform key; store index in region and provide customer download link.
- E2E test harness: synthetic traffic generator that asserts 99.99% of pinned requests stay in-region; run during onboarding and monthly.

Fallback scenarios (operator playbook):
- Soft fallback (preferred): when local capacity < threshold (default 5%), route to warm-standby region and flag the request with a compliance tag; auto-create incident and notify customer with timeframe estimate.
- Hard enforcement: block new requests when SLO to be maintained and capacity cannot be expanded; return 451-like error code and instruction to retry.
- Customer choice: allow customers to select soft fallback, hard block, or manual approval for fallback in contract.

Customer-impact stories (anecdotal notes from pilot):
- FinServ customer in EU: requested compute residency. During initial staging, we discovered that telemetry exports (central logging) caused metadata egress; resolved by offering region-scoped logging buckets plus a logging-forwarder agent. Time to remediate: 3 days.
- Health-tech pilot: required per-request evidence; generated large index files (~50GB/month) for the residency index when traffic is high. Cost estimate: +$1.2k/month per 1M requests for storage+signing.

Implementation decisions to track (open items):
- Evidence format: JSON-lines vs Protobuf? Tradeoffs: readable vs compact. Action: pick JSON-lines for month 1 for debuggability. (Owner: Liam)
- Retention policy defaults: 90 days vs 365 days. Legal leaning: 365; infra cost team prefers 90. (Owner: Legal + Priya)
- Signed index key management: use customer-supplied key (preferred) or Redwood-managed key? If customer supplies, we must accept public key only and not hold private key. (Owner: Security)

Edge cases and gotchas (notes to self):
- Third-party plugins calling outbound APIs can leak PII—require outbound egress review checklist.
- Model updates: if model download/weights fetch is from central registry, ensure registry has regional mirrors; otherwise downloads may cross borders.
- Backup snapshots: snapshots may be replicated for durability—need explicit opt-in for cross-region replication.

Action items & owners (near-term):
- Draft SOW appendix with three commitment tiers and price multipliers (Priya, Legal) — due 2024-10-01.
- Small PoC: build residency-index job for one dedicated EU tenant and run for 30 days (Liam) — due 2024-10-20.
- Update onboarding checklist (Solutions eng) with required config knobs for "no-fallback" mode (Sofia) — due 2024-09-30.
- Create egress-test suite and add to nightly CI (Noah + SRE) — due 2024-10-15.

Open questions for next sync:
- What SLO degradation is permissible when a customer has strict hard-block? (ops vs sales trade).
- How aggressive should our default fallback policy be for new enterprise customers?
- Billing model for evidence exports: should signed indices be an add-on?

References & pointers:
- Confluence spec (linked above) for geo controls implementation notes.
- Jira: ENG-2145 (regional routing fallbacks) — contains earlier experiment logs.
- Infra PR: #487 — region mirror work done last quarter.

Notes-to-self / scribbles:
- Keep customers able to choose tradeoffs; don't overpromise per-request audit unless they pay for it.
- Consider an "evidence-as-service" add-on for customers who want compliance reports delivered monthly as signed archives.

Status: draft; will convert to partial-final once PoC completes and Legal signs off on clause language.

-- end --
